existing_eitza_edges_in_dataset.note: Innovating in Torah LEADS TO rectification of impure thoughts — this is cause-and-effect, correctly typed as eitza.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.note: The central practice recommended: studying the Rebbe's Torah and deriving chiddushim from it. Equivalent to dataset node 'לחדש איזה דבר בתורה'.

Explicitly stated as the bechina of chiddush in Torah: 'שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת מְדַמֶּה מִלְּתָא לְמִלְּתָא'. Torah innovation inherently involves comparing and connecting concepts — this IS the rectified use of the imaginative faculty.
The faculty that generates impure thoughts (hirhurim), but when used for Torah chiddush it becomes rectified. This is a neutral concept — it can serve good (Torah innovation) or evil (hirhurim).
Come through the koach hamedameh. Rectified by innovating in Torah. Partially present as 'תקון גדול להרהורים' in the eitza edge.
Torah chiddush is described as 'a great tikkun for the past' — a separate benefit beyond rectifying hirhurim.
Torah chiddush is also a benefit for the souls of one's departed ancestors.
